english: Grandmother, I have come to you. Grandson, you have grown! Is your mother well? She is well, and she sent you wool. Sit by me, and I will tell you a story. Tell me the story of my grandfather! Your grandfather was a great man, and he struck down a bear with a stone.

english: Man of this house, the king calls you to the assembly. When shall I arrive? Arrive at dawn! Why does the king call the men? Enemies drove away the cattle of the village. I and my brothers shall come. Drink mead with me, and then go! Let me drink, and let me praise the giver.

english: Mother, why are you sweeping the house? Guests are coming from your grandmother's village. Kindle the fire, and set the pot over it. How many guests are coming? Three men and four women. Shall I fetch water from the spring? Fetch water, and milk the cows. Let me run!

english: Woman, Dawn has grown bright, and I am returning home. Do not go, guest! Eat with us first. I am satisfied. My wife is waiting for me. Then take this garment. It is snowing in the hills. You are dear to me. May you be fortunate! Be well, and come to us again!

pie: kʷíd méh₂ter gʰóstis h₂Hséh₂i h₁épi sédyeti? h₁éy deywóybʰos lewbʰós. dyḗws h₁ím pn̥th₁sú spéḱyeti. h₁éy dʰéh₁s? h₁éy ne dʰéh₁s. deywṓs gʰósteyes de gʷm̥sḱónti. nu moy h₁ésmey sédos déh₃oh₂. h₁íd dh₃dʰí h₁ésmey-kʷe péh₃tlom h₁opéye.
english: Mother, why does the guest sit by the hearth? He is dear to the gods. Sky sees him on the paths. Is he a god? He is not a god. But gods come as guests. Then I will give him my seat. Give it, and hand him the cup!

pie: dáyh₂wer moy yugóm Hrumptó. yugóm moy toy dh₃dʰí h₂éǵrom moy h₂érh₃yoh₂. h₁íd h₁m̥dʰí h₁íd-kʷe wékʷsperoy h₂ew wéǵʰontu. ugʷsénes toy h₂yuHn̥ḱṓs? h₁éyes h₂yuHn̥ḱṓs. nu h₁íns yugdʰí h₁íns-kʷe mē stunéds. ǵr̥h₂nóm toy yéh₁ni dédeh₃oh₂.
english: Brother-in-law, my yoke broke. Give me your yoke; I am ploughing my field. Take it, and bring it back in the evening. Are your oxen young? They are young. Then yoke them, and do not strike them. At harvest I will give you grain.

pie: swésor démi h₁ési? démi h₁ésmi h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂m-kʷe téksmi. wiḱdʰí sddʰí-kʷe. ne sédoh₂. gʷówes moy gʰórtōd bʰugént. h₁íns dedórḱth₂e? gʷṓs déh₂newi h₂éyeri dedórḱh₂e. moḱs gʷh₂dʰí dyḗws-kʷe te h₁uHyéh₁t. h₁éymi. ḱóymos toy kéh₂ilos h₁syéh₁t.
english: Sister, are you at home? I am at home, and I am weaving wool. Come in and sit down! I shall not sit down. My cattle have fled from the enclosure. Have you seen them? I have seen cattle at the river in the morning. Go quickly, and may Sky help you! I am going. May your household be whole!

pie: gʷr̥Hḗi h₂ówis, kʷésyo wlh₂néH ne (h₁é) est, h₁éḱwons spéḱet, h₁oinom gʰe gʷr̥Húm wóǵʰom wéǵʰontm̥ h₁oinom-kʷe méǵHm bʰórom, h₁oinom-kʷe ǵʰménm̥ Hṓḱu bʰérontm̥.
english: A sheep that had no wool saw horses, one of them pulling a heavy wagon, one carrying a big load, and one carrying a man quickly.

pie: h₂éwh₂e toy wĺ̥kʷos h₂ówim h₁épt. kúdʰe wĺ̥kʷos h₁íh₂m̥ h₁épt? h₁íh₂m̥ pr̥kʷéwi h₁épi h₂ewsér h₁épt. wĺ̥kʷom swṓys h₃kʷbʰís widés? h₁ím widóm h₁éy méǵh₂s h₁ést. népotn̥s moy ǵʰuHéye h₁ím-kʷe wrégōmes. tébʰye ḱóm gʷm̥yéh₁m̥? gʷm̥dʰí ǵʰoysóm-kʷe toy h₁m̥dʰí.
english: Uncle, a wolf has seized a sheep of yours! Where did the wolf seize it? He seized it by the oak at dawn. Did you see the wolf with your own eyes? I saw him; he was big. Call my nephews, and let us hunt him. Might I come with you? Come, and take your spear.

pie: kʷósmōd ǵénh₁esos gʰóstipotey ǵn̥h₁yéth₂e? sénōd ǵénh₁esos ǵn̥h₁yóh₂e. ḱód sédos swéh₂bʰis ǵʰesr̥bʰís démom. kʷésyo népōts túH? h₁eǵóh₂ déh₂newi poh₂imnés népōts. h₁ésyo méh₂term̥ h₃rēǵés dʰugh₂tḗr h₁ést. nu toy ǵénh₁os ḱlutóm. méǵh₂i sédesi sddʰí.
english: Host, from which lineage were you born? I was born from an old lineage. I built this dwelling with my own hands. Whose descendant are you? I am the grandson of a herdsman by the river. His mother was the daughter of a king. Then your lineage is famous. Sit on the great seat!

pie: eḱwos wewekur, "ḱludʰe, owei! ḱerd angʰetai widontbʰyos: ǵʰm̥on, potis, wl̥nam owiyōm kʷr̥neti soi gʷʰermom westrom; owibʰyos kʷe wl̥nā ne esti".
english: The horses said: "Listen, sheep, our hearts pain us when we see this: a man, the master, makes the wool of the sheep into a warm garment for himself. And the sheep has no wool."

english: Wife, I have come! You have returned unharmed! The children wept at night. How was the road? The road was long, and the rivers were cold. Are the cattle alive? They are alive, and the herd has grown. Sit down, and I will cook you food. Your words are sweeter than honey.

english: Friend, where are you going? I am going home; my wife and children are waiting for me. Man, what is your name? I am Man-Minded. I seek the house of the king. It is on the hill. Walk with me to my village! I walk with you.

english: I have stayed many days in your house. Now let me return home. Winter is here, and snow lies on the paths. Stay here in winter; in spring go! I devour much of your food. We have much grain. And we rejoice in your songs. Then I shall stay, and I shall sing.

english: Old man, sing us a song of the old heroes! I sing of the hero who slew the serpent. His fame is imperishable. Who was he? He was Of-Goodly-Fame. Now you sing! I do not know the old songs. Let me sing a herdsman's song.

english: Mistress, my fire has gone out. Give me burning wood from your hearth! Why did it go out? My daughter lay down, and she did not guard it. Take it, and carry it quickly to your house! You are a giver of good things. Afterwards you will give me fire.

english: Young man, my horse is thirsty. I shall lead him to the river. Does he eat barley? He eats barley and grass. He is a swift horse. Where did you acquire him? I acquired him from a king for ten sheep. Your horse is swifter than my horses.

english: Host, I am leaving your house on this day. Take this cup, a gift! When you drink from it, remember us. When you come to my village, I will receive you in my house. We two are friends; let us not forget it. May the gods guard you on the road!

english: Old man, do you know me? I do not know you. Who is your father? My father is Of-True-Fame. He sat at your hearth, and you gave him a cup. Now I remember! You are the son of my guest. Be dear to us, and stay in our house! Let me stay, and let me give you a gift.

english: Friend, you received me as a brother. Take this spear from my hand. I take it, and I give you my horse. Let us two set down a pledge: our descendants shall be friends. May Father Sky hear our pledge! Whoever breaks it, may he strike that one down!

english: Woman, I am freezing. The snow covered the path. Come in quickly, and get warm by the fire! Where were you going in the night? I was going to my sister's house. It is far. Sleep here this night! Give me warm milk! Drink, and may your heart grow warm!

english: Woman, who is the master of this house? My husband, Of-Divine-Race, dwells here. He is ploughing the field. Whom do you seek? I seek a roof for the night. I am weary. Wait at the door! Let me call my husband. I am staying here. Drink this water!

pie: ǵŕ̥h₂enti mē gʰrémes HréwdHmi. kʷíd HréwdHsi? swéḱuros moy ǵʰiméni mért h₁ím-kʷe ne widóm. ḱéh₂dos toy ḱérdi ḱéyor. píph₃e h₁ím-kʷe memn̥dʰí. h₁ésyo toy h₁nómn̥ h₁éh₃si gʷíh₃weti. wékʷesh₂ toy moy h₁wésuh₂.
english: Old woman, do not be angry: I am weeping. Why are you weeping? My father-in-law died in the winter, and I did not see him. Grief lies on your heart. Drink, and remember him. His name lives in your mouth. Your words are good to me.

english: Grandfather, what does the master of the house owe a guest? He gives him water, food and a seat. The guest eats. Then the master asks his name. What does the guest owe? He owes the master a gift and sweet words. He does not steal from the house. Who guards him on the way? Sky guards him. He hears his words.

pie: dʰúgh₂ter déh₂nu h₁idʰé pr̥yéh₁m̥? h₁idʰé mē pérs. wódr̥ dʰubʰróm gʰrémeti-kʷe. pérwr̥ pr̥kʷúsu Hn̥dʰér h₁ésti. kúdʰe wódr̥ bʰéresi? h₁íd moy dṓm bʰéroh₂ h₂énHos moy mā́dsom pékʷeti. h₁mé sékʷeso nu-kʷe pr̥dʰí. túH ḱéyweh₂.
english: Maiden, might I cross the river here? Do not cross here! The water is deep, and it roars. There is a ford below the oaks. Where are you carrying the water? I am carrying it to my house; my grandmother is cooking food. Follow me, and then cross! You are friendly.

pie: gʰóstipotey kʷid léh₂kt. só h₂énh₁mos stégesos Hyowdʰéyeti. só ne wĺ̥kʷos? ḱwónes th₂kéh₁yonti. l̥gʰdʰí ssdʰí-kʷe h₁eǵóh₂ bʰéwdʰoh₂. túH n̥smé h₂léksesi. h₂ewsér h₂éḱh₃omes.
english: Host, something made a noise. That is the wind; it is shaking the roof. Is it not a wolf? The dogs are silent. Lie down and sleep; I am awake. You guard us. At dawn let us eat.

english: Sister, do you not know me? I have not seen you. Who are you, man? I am your brother. I left our father's house as a boy. Show me your hand! A bear tore my brother's hand. This hand the bear tore. Now I know you, brother! Come in! Our mother will weep with joy.

pie: owis nu eḱwobʰ(y)os (eḱwomos) ewewkʷet, "ḱēr agʰnutoi moi eḱwōns aǵontm̥ nerm̥ widn̥tei".
english: The sheep said to the horses: "My heart pains me, seeing a man driving horses."
